name: _sparse_addmm
description: Representative ATen schema, copied verbatim and not an exclusive ABI: aten::_sparse_addmm(Tensor self, Tensor mat1, Tensor mat2, *, Scalar beta=1, Scalar alpha=1) -> Tensor. All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: aten::_sparse_addmm(Tensor self, Tensor mat1, Tensor mat2, *, Scalar beta=1, Scalar alpha=1) -> Tensor ; aten::_sparse_addmm.out(Tensor self, Tensor mat1, Tensor mat2, *, Scalar beta=1, Scalar alpha=1, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). The original Gems pytest owns the full contract for overload selection, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation; this definition represents one overload only and the tests must not be narrowed to it. In particular the .out overload is exercised directly with a keyword-only out buffer and the candidate must return that same buffer, while the default overload is exercised through the public injected entrypoint. The optional beta and alpha defaults are the ATen schema defaults (1 and 1), retained here as JSON numbers. Semantics derived from the tests: result = beta * self + alpha * (mat1 @ mat2), where self is a dense Tensor broadcast to (mat1.size(0), mat2.size(1)) (including 1-D, 1-sized row/column and 0-dim scalar-broadcast forms), mat1 is a 2-D sparse operand (uncoalesced or coalesced COO with duplicate coordinates, explicitly stored zeros or zero nnz, and CSR) and mat2 is a 2-D dense operand that may carry a non-contiguous stride or non-zero storage offset. beta scales the dense addend elementwise and alpha scales the sparse-dense product; the tested dtype set is float32 and complex64, with float64 added only when the build reports the static FP64 capability flag, and the sparse operand is coalesced by the operator. Gradients are defined for all three operands (the sparse operand gradient is itself a coalesced COO). Unsupported dtypes are rejected with RuntimeError on the measured NVIDIA vendor only, where the exact rejected set is a property of that vendor and dtypes are listed only when this build can construct their operands; invalid operand shapes are rejected with RuntimeError.
